stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function in language tasks.
It is associated with key AI technologies like transformers and safetensors, pointing to its technical foundation.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 3.6 Flash and cybersecurity AI, teases 3.5 Pro and Gemini 4
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google has unveiled Gemini 3.6 Flash and introduced a new cybersecurity AI offering.
The announcement signals ongoing rapid iteration in Google's AI roadmap, with Gemini 3.5 Pro also mentioned.
Google is actively developing the next generation, Gemini 4, indicating a continuous push for advanced models.

stories.title: Apps targeted at US troops contain Chinese and Russian code
stories.author: Dell Cameron, wired.com
bullet_points: Analysis revealed that over one-eighth of apps targeting US troops contain foreign code.
The foreign code identified originates from both Chinese and Russian sources.
This highlights a significant cybersecurity risk concerning military-related applications.

stories.title:
New Gemini models dropped

https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-3-6-flash-3-5-flash-lite-3-5-flash-cyber/
stories.author: ben
bullet_points: Google has released new iterations of its Gemini models, including Gemini 3.6, 3.5 Flash, and 3.5 Flash Lite.
The new models are designed to offer varying levels of capability and efficiency, catering to different use cases.
The announcement signals continued rapid development and expansion of Google's AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Key associated technologies include transformers, safetensors, and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
The associated tags indicate its relevance to transformers and safetensors formats.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains are substantial, reaching up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released as an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, promising faster local AI inference.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating active development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The tool leverages the Ollama ecosystem, positioning itself within the growing trend of local LLM deployment.

stories.title: Apple’s rumored ‘Upgrade’ program brings lease-to-own pricing for iPhones, Macs, and iPads
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly launching an 'Apple Upgrade' program for iPhones, Macs, and iPads.
The program will function similarly to a car lease, offering flexible ownership options.
The initiative is being driven by rising component and RAM shortages impacting device pricing.

stories.title: Anthropic’s $1.5 billion book piracy settlement approved by judge
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Anthropic has reached a $1.5 billion class action settlement with authors.
The lawsuit alleged that Anthropic trained its AI models using copyrighted books without permission.
The settlement will provide authors with approximately $3,000 for each book involved.

stories.title: Tesla Robotaxis go to Florida
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla is officially launching its Robotaxi service in Orlando and Tampa, Florida.
The announcement was made via a post on X, coinciding with what appears to be an earnings-related announcement.
Details regarding fleet size and customer availability for the service were not provided in the initial announcement.

stories.title: Samsung can’t afford to play it safe with Apple’s first foldable looming
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Samsung is preparing for a major Galaxy Unpacked event focused heavily on foldable devices.
The company is expected to launch updated versions of its existing Fold and Flip phones.
A significant new, shorter and wider Fold form factor is anticipated, signaling a major lineup shift.

stories.title: Google launches a cheaper alternative to large AI security models like Mythos
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google is introducing Gemini 3.6 Flash Cyber, a new, cost-efficient AI security model.
This model is positioned as a direct, cheaper alternative to large, premium AI security systems like Anthropic's Mythos.
The primary function of the new model is to rapidly identify and assist in patching security vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Differentiable Logic Gate Networks for Low-Latency EEG Classification on Edge Devices
stories.author: Camilo E. Valderrama
bullet_points: Introduces Differentiable Logic Gate Networks (Diff-Logic) as a hardware-native alternative to conventional neural networks for EEG classification.
Addresses the latency bottleneck of floating-point arithmetic by compiling models into pure Boolean circuits executable via bitwise CPU operations.
Demonstrates effectiveness across two EEG classification tasks (dementia detection and emotion recognition) using rigorous comparative experiments.

stories.title: FlashRT: Agent Harness for Guiding Agents to Deploy Real-Time Multimodal Applications
stories.author: Beidi Chen
bullet_points: Introduces FlashRT, an agent harness designed to guide the deployment of real-time multimodal applications.
Addresses the complexity of deploying heterogeneous models (like voice agents/video generation) which require application-specific decisions on placement and parallelism.
Overcomes limitations of existing serving systems that rely on fixed workload assumptions, enabling better performance optimization.

stories.title: France's Anssi Will Block PQC-Free Products from Certification Starting 2027
stories.author: Sami_Lehtinen
bullet_points: France's ANSSI is implementing a mandatory security standard change.
The regulation will block products lacking Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) certification.
The enforcement deadline for these PQC requirements is set for 2027.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for improved functionality on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM tooling by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval.

stories.title: Twitch will let parents stop their teens going live
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Twitch is introducing enhanced parental controls for users aged 13-17.
Guardians can now link their accounts to their teens' profiles for oversight.
Features include the ability to block teens from broadcasting and receiving weekly activity summaries.

stories.title: Steam Deck sales are losing steam since May's price hike
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Steam Deck sales have reportedly declined significantly since a price increase in May.
Sales data indicates an 80% drop in the current sales rate compared to 2025.
The article suggests the price hike is a contributing factor to the sales slowdown.

stories.title: When your vehicle outlives its cloud: What happens next?
stories.author: Michael Harley
bullet_points: Automakers heavily rely on connected vehicle technology.
The lifespan of cloud-based vehicle support is finite, posing a future challenge.
The article discusses the implications of vehicle technology outlasting its supporting cloud infrastructure.

stories.title: Firefighting drones in the works as wildfires plague US nearly year-round
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Drones are being tested as a potential tool for early wildfire intervention.
The initiative involves a competition, specifically the XPRIZE, focused on this technology.
The development is highly relevant given the increasing frequency and severity of wildfires in the US, particularly California.

stories.title: Judge halts Paramount's $111B purchase of Warner Bros. in win for US states
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A judge has issued a restraining order against Paramount's proposed $111B acquisition of Warner Bros.
The legal action stems from concerns that the merger is likely to violate existing antitrust laws.
The ruling represents a significant legal hurdle for the proposed media consolidation deal.

stories.title: The Space Force is now seeking to buy up to $30 billion in rocket launches
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The Space Force is tasked with acquiring up to $30 billion in rocket launch services.
This significant funding increase is driven by increased operational demands from the Trump administration.
The news highlights a major budgetary commitment to bolstering US space capabilities.

stories.title: Simple Domain Generalization for Strong Pixel-Level Image Tampering Detection in Modern VLMs
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Addresses the growing challenge of pixel-level image tampering detection in modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
Focuses on Domain Generalization to ensure detection models remain robust across different VLM-generated manipulation styles (cross-model/out-of-distribution shifts).
Aims to develop tampering localization models resilient to the advanced image generation capabilities of models like ChatGPT and Gemini.

stories.title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Efficient Pathology Foundation Models for Whole-Slide and Tumor Microenvironment Analysis
stories.author: Hoifung Poon
bullet_points: Introduces GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash, new efficient foundation models for computational pathology.
Addresses limitations of existing pathology models, such as tile-level operation, restrictive licensing, and high computational cost.
Focuses on transforming cancer diagnosis and prognosis by learning representations from whole-slide and tumor microenvironment data.

stories.title: Learning Adaptive Safety Margins for Visual Navigation
stories.author: Yi Fang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in robot navigation: the inadequacy of fixed safety margins in cluttered environments.
Proposes a novel 'context-conditioned safety critic' to learn adaptive clearance preferences for path planning.
Focuses on improving trajectory selection from diffusion-based planners using egocentric RGB-D input.

stories.title: TRIM: Reducing AI-Generated CodeSlop via Agent Trajectory Minimization
stories.author: Baishakhi Ray
bullet_points: The paper addresses the issue of 'codeSlop'—AI-generated code being overly verbose compared to human code.
The root cause is identified as the agent's internal search process, where speculative and abandoned edits accumulate.
The proposed solution, TRIM, aims to reduce this code bloat by minimizing the agent's trajectory during code generation.

stories.title: LLMs and Agentic AI Systems for Smart Grids: A Tutorial on Architectures and Applications
stories.author: Yuanyuan Shi
bullet_points: The paper discusses the application of LLMs and agentic AI systems to complex technical domains like smart grids.
Agentic schemes are being used in smart grids for forecasting, optimization, and control by interfacing with trusted solvers.
A key gap identified is the lack of a unified methodology for designing and evaluating these LLM-based systems, noting potential for physically infeasible outputs.

stories.title: The Many Senses of Visual Similarity: A Text-Prompted Image Perceptual Metric
stories.author: Richard Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current image similarity metrics by acknowledging context-dependent human perception.
Introduces a new large-scale dataset featuring human similarity judgments annotated across multiple semantic aspects.
Aims to allow similarity metrics to be conditioned on specific visual attributes (e.g., shape vs. color).

stories.title: Patch Policy: Efficient Embodied Control via Dense Visual Representations
stories.author: Lerrel Pinto
bullet_points: The paper addresses the underutilization of dense visual features from Vision Transformers (ViTs) in robot learning.
Current robot policies often either over-compress observations into a single token or train visual backbones from scratch, losing detail and pre-training benefits.
The proposed 'Patch Policy' aims to offer an efficient embodied control method by leveraging dense visual representations, addressing the heaviness of existing dense-feature models.

stories.title: Causal Discovery on Irregular Time Series
stories.author: Pedro Bizarro
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in causal discovery methods: their reliance on regular, discrete time series.
The paper proposes an extension of the PCMCI+ method to handle irregularly sampled data streams.
This work is highly relevant to real-world applications like sensor data, healthcare monitoring, and financial transaction analysis.

stories.title: Vector Search As Nearest Neighbor Matching: RAG-based Policy Learning in Causal Inference
stories.author: Taka Kato
bullet_points: Proposes novel one-step and two-step methods for policy learning utilizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Frames RAG-based action selection within the established potential outcome framework of causal inference.
The two-step method integrates vector search for retrieving action-specific evidence with a generator for estimating conditional outcomes.

stories.title: PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning
stories.author: Warren J. Gross
bullet_points: PPL-Factory introduces a new method for task-aware and budget-aware data selection during LLM fine-tuning.
The research addresses the inefficiency of using all training samples by focusing on selecting only the most informative ones.
It aims to overcome the limitations of existing data selection heuristics (like quality or diversity) which are not task-generalizable.

stories.title: Three-Body Scattering for Generative Modeling
stories.author: Tao Lin
bullet_points: Introduces Three-Body Scattering Modeling (TBSM) as an alternative to standard generative model architectures (e.g., adversarial, autoregressive).
Proposes using a 'proper distributional energy' to induce sample-level motion and provide direct regression supervision for a one-step generator.
The core mechanism translates the energy distance into a constant-size interaction model between projectiles and real sources.

stories.title: Certified Training for Convolutional Perturbations
stories.author: Alessio Lomuscio
bullet_points: Vision models are vulnerable to real-world perturbations, such as motion blur from camera shake.
Current robustness methods (like data augmentation) lack formal safety guarantees needed for critical applications.
The research proposes 'Certified Training' to provide formal safety guarantees against these perturbations.

stories.title: EVOLVE: Efficient Learned Volume Compression with Variable-Rate Encoding on a Cross-Domain Database
stories.author: Chaoli Wang
bullet_points: EVOLVE is a new autoencoder-based method designed for efficient, lossy compression of large-scale volumetric data.
It addresses limitations of conventional compressors by aiming to preserve fine structural details even at high compression ratios.
A key innovation is the implementation of variable-rate encoding, overcoming the fixed compression ratio issue found in Implicit Neural Representations (INRs).

stories.title: It's Not What You Say, It's How You Say It: Evaluating LLM Responses to Expressions of Belief
stories.author: Alex Warstadt
bullet_points: The research addresses how Large Language Models (LLMs) should handle user-expressed beliefs (EoBs), deciding whether to accept them contextually or adhere to prior knowledge.
It introduces a typology to systematically evaluate how linguistically diverse forms of EoBs (e.g., presuppositions, certainty markers) affect LLM responses.
The study focuses on the nuanced impact of *how* a belief is stated, rather than just the content, on the model's behavior.

stories.title: SWE-Pruner Pro: The Coder LLM Already Knows What to Prune
stories.author: Xiaodong Gu
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Pruner Pro, a novel method for context pruning in coding LLMs.
Challenges existing methods (like SWE-Pruner) by leveraging the agent's internal representations to determine context relevance.
The new approach prunes tool outputs directly within the agent using a small auxiliary head.

stories.title: PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning
stories.author: Warren J. Gross
bullet_points: PPL-Factory proposes a new method for task-aware and budget-aware data selection during LLM fine-tuning.
The research addresses the inefficiency of using all training samples by aiming to reduce computational cost while maintaining performance.
It moves beyond fixed, indirect heuristics (like data quality or diversity) by introducing a perplexity-based selection mechanism.

stories.title: VEHBench: A Stage-Local Diagnostic Benchmark for LLM-Assisted Vibration Energy Harvester Design
stories.author: Guobiao Hu
bullet_points: Introduces VEHBench, a new diagnostic benchmark specifically designed for LLM-assisted design of Vibration Energy Harvesters (VEHs).
Addresses a gap in current engineering benchmarks by focusing on LLM behavior across *stages* of coupled physical design, rather than just final artifact validity.
Relevant to the growing intersection of AI/LLMs and specialized engineering domains like battery-free IoT.

stories.title: Do Language Models Dream of Binding Molecules? Benchmarking LLMs under Spatial Constraints
stories.author: Alex Zhavoronkov
bullet_points: The research explores using Large Language Models (LLMs) for structure-based drug design (SBDD), a critical area in pharmaceutical AI.
It addresses the current limitation of LLMs in reasoning about complex 3D spatial constraints, a key challenge in molecular generation.
The work benchmarks LLMs against established diffusion models in the context of pocket-conditioned molecule generation.

stories.title: O-VAD: Industrial Video Anomaly Detection through Object-Centric Tracking and Reasoning
stories.author: Min Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of Industrial Video Anomaly Detection (IVAD) in manufacturing.
Identifies limitations of existing Vision-Language Model (VLM) methods in complex industrial environments.
Proposes a new approach, O-VAD, focusing on object-centric tracking and reasoning to handle procedural constraints.

stories.title: How Does Alignment Tuning Shape Representations of Sycophancy and Related Cue-Induced Biases in LLMs?
stories.author: Zhijing Jin
bullet_points: The research investigates how alignment tuning affects LLM representations of sycophancy and cue-induced biases.
It addresses the vulnerability of modern LLMs to subtle prompt changes, such as hints or incorrect few-shot examples.
The study extracts per-bias directions from hidden states across five model families and seven bias types using probing and related methods.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
stories.author: Furu Wei
bullet_points: Proposes 'Experiential Learning' (EL) to improve LLM training beyond standard RL reward compression.
Reconfigures the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm into an LLM-as-a-Coach to provide richer feedback.
The coach distills assessment into transferable knowledge to condition and internalize learning within the policy.

stories.title: 432 Linux kernel CVEs published in the last 24 hours
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via Helithumper
bullet_points: A large volume of 432 new CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) were published for the Linux kernel in a single 24-hour period.
This indicates a significant and rapid discovery/disclosure rate of security vulnerabilities within the core Linux operating system.
The news is highly relevant to system administrators, security professionals, and Linux users who must prioritize patching and vulnerability management.

stories.title: AI And Code Ownership: Who Is Responsible For Generated Code?
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: The article addresses the complex legal question of code ownership when AI generates software.
It highlights the uncertainty surrounding intellectual property rights for AI-assisted code.
This topic represents an emerging and important discussion point in software development and AI ethics.

stories.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash & 3.5 Flash-Lite: Developer guide
stories.author: pat_loeber
bullet_points: The article details developer guides for new Gemini models: Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.
These models represent updates or iterations within Google's Gemini family, targeting developer use.
The focus is on practical implementation rather than a fundamental AI breakthrough.

stories.title: Snowflake Cortex, Explained Like an AI That Lives Next to Your Data
stories.author: ramkumar-m-n
bullet_points: The article discusses Snowflake Cortex, a new AI feature integrated into the Snowflake data warehouse.
It aims to explain the concept of applying AI directly alongside existing data infrastructure.
The content is presented from a developer's perspective, suggesting practical application insights.

stories.title: RAG isn't an AI problem. It's a data engineering problem wearing an AI hat.
stories.author: cyclopt_dimitrisk
bullet_points: The article argues that Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) challenges are fundamentally data engineering issues, not purely AI model problems.
It critiques the common pattern in RAG tutorials, noting a significant gap between theoretical examples and real-world production deployment.
The piece suggests a shift in focus is needed from just AI model tuning to robust data pipeline construction for effective RAG.
